title: 4 Keys Keyboard
summary: Consider a keyboard with the keys A, Ctrl-A, Ctrl-C, and Ctrl-V.
statement: Consider a keyboard with the keys A, Ctrl-A, Ctrl-C, and Ctrl-V. The key A prints 'A' on the screen. The Ctrl-A key selects the entire screen content. The Ctrl-C key copies the selected content to the buffer. The Ctrl-V key pastes the content of the buffer at the end of the screen. Given an integer n, determine the maximum number of 'A's that can be printed with no more than n key presses.
constraints: Use A, Ctrl-A, Ctrl-C, and Ctrl-V to maximize the final number of As in at most n key presses.
hints: An optimal copy phase starts from a previously optimal screen.
Try every breakpoint before Ctrl-A, Ctrl-C, and the remaining pastes.
dp[i]=max(i, dp[j]*(i-j-1)) for valid earlier j.
After the breakpoint, two setup keys preserve the screen and every remaining paste adds one saved copy.
editorial: After the breakpoint, two setup keys preserve the screen and every remaining paste adds one saved copy.

tests.explanation: Pressing A three times produces three As.
Type AAA, select all, copy, and paste twice to produce nine As.
